# `tlgr auth`

11 operations. Every one takes the global flags (`--json`, `--plain`, `-a/--account`, `--results-only`, `--select`, `--dry-run`, `--yes`, `--no-input`, `--flood-wait-max`, `-v`) anywhere on the line.

| [`auth login-email set`](#tlgr-auth-login-email-set) | Set, verify or reset the login email the server demands during login |
| [`auth qr`](#tlgr-auth-qr) | Log in by QR code: print the tg://login token and wait for approval |

| [`auth reset-account`](#tlgr-auth-reset-account) | Delete an account you can no longer log into (last resort) |
| [`auth send-code`](#tlgr-auth-send-code) | Start a phone login: ask Telegram to send a login code |
| [`auth sign-up`](#tlgr-auth-sign-up) | Register a new account for a phone whose code was already verified |

### `auth autologin-url get`

Append the autologin token to a telegram.org URL.

```
tlgr auth autologin-url get <URL> [OPTIONS]
```

**returns `AutologinUrl`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `URL` | text | yes | A telegram.org URL to sign into. |

```console
$ tlgr auth autologin-url get https://telegram.org/faq --json
```

### `auth qr`

Log in by QR code: print the tg://login token and wait for approval.

Streams a frame per token and re-exports on expiry. Telethon follows `auth.loginTokenMigrateTo` to the target DC itself, which is the step a hand-rolled QR login usually forgets.

```
tlgr auth qr [OPTIONS]
```

**mutating · runs without an account · returns `Page[QrLogin]`**

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--alias` | text |  | Account alias to create. |
| `--api-hash` | text |  | api_hash for this account. |
| `--api-id` | int |  | api_id for this account. |
| `--password` | text |  | The 2FA cloud password. |
| `--test-dc` | flag |  | Use the Telegram test DCs. |
| `--url-only` | flag |  | Print only the tg://login URL (pipe it into qrencode). |
| `--wait` | text | `5m` | Give up after this long. |

```console
$ tlgr auth qr --alias work --json
```

### `auth send-code`

Start a phone login: ask Telegram to send a login code.

Writes the pending login (phone + phone_code_hash + code type) to `login-state.json` at 0600, so `auth verify-code` is a separate command in a separate process. `type` is reported verbatim — a third-party api_id normally gets `app`, meaning the code lands in another logged-in Telegram session rather than an SMS.

```
tlgr auth send-code <PHONE> [OPTIONS]
```

**mutating · runs without an account · returns `SentCode`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PHONE` | text | yes | The number to log in with. |

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--alias` | text |  | Account alias to create or resume (default: the last 6 digits). |
| `--allow-flashcall` | flag |  | Permit a flash-call code; you type the number. |
| `--allow-missed-call` | flag |  | Permit a missed-call code (read the caller id). |
| `--api-hash` | text |  | api_hash — never on the command line. |
| `--api-id` | int |  | api_id; else TLGR_API_ID, then the config. |
| `--current-number` | flag |  | codeSettings.current_number: this device owns it. |
| `--no-future-tokens` | flag |  | Do not offer stored tokens; force a real code. |
| `--recaptcha-token` | text |  | A reCAPTCHA token you solved. |
| `--test-dc` | flag |  | Log in against the Telegram test DCs. |

```console
$ tlgr auth send-code +989123456789 --json
```

### `auth sign-up`

Register a new account for a phone whose code was already verified.

A separate command, never a fallback: a login that finds no account stops with `signup_required` rather than creating one. Third-party api_ids often get PHONE_NUMBER_APP_SIGNUP_FORBIDDEN, reported as-is.

```
tlgr auth sign-up [OPTIONS]
```

**mutating · runs without an account · returns `LoginResult`**

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--accept-tos` | flag |  | Accept the Terms of Service returned by auth.signIn. |
| `--alias` | text |  | Which pending login. |
| `--first-name` | text |  | Required. |
| `--last-name` | text |  | Optional. |
| `--no-joined-notifications` | flag |  | Do not tell contacts that you joined. |

```console
$ tlgr auth sign-up --first-name Ada --accept-tos --json
```

### `auth tos`

Show, accept or decline the Terms of Service.

The daemon polls `help.getTermsOfServiceUpdate` at the returned `expires` and flags a pending update in its status; accepting is always an explicit run of this command.

```
tlgr auth tos [OPTIONS]
```

**mutating · returns `Terms`**

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--accept` | flag |  | Accept the pending Terms of Service. |
| `--confirm-age` | int |  | Confirm your age when asked. |
| `--decline` | flag |  | Decline — this deletes the account. |
| `--delete-account` | flag |  | Acknowledge that declining deletes the account. |

Also invocable as: `tlgr account terms`

```console
$ tlgr auth tos --json
```

### `auth verify-code`

Finish a pending login: submit the code and, if asked, the password.

The password never appears in argv. SRP is recomputed against a fresh `account.getPassword` when the server answers SRP_ID_INVALID, and a word or phrase code is passed through unchanged — validating it as digits is how a client breaks `sentCodeTypeSmsWord`.

```
tlgr auth verify-code [CODE] [OPTIONS]
```

**mutating · runs without an account · returns `LoginResult`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CODE` | text | no | Digits, an SMS word/phrase, or a t.me/login/<code> link. '-' reads stdin. |

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--alias` | text |  | Which pending login to finish. |
| `--apple-token` | text |  | Apple id-token for the login email. |
| `--code-hash` | text |  | Override the stored phone_code_hash. |
| `--email-code` | text |  | Login-email code instead of a phone code. |
| `--google-token` | text |  | Google id-token for the login email. |
| `--password` | text |  | The 2FA cloud password. |
| `--phone` | text |  | Override the pending login state. |

```console
$ tlgr auth verify-code 12345 --json
```
